\begin{proof}
Let $U$ be any neighborhood of $x$. Select an open neighborhood $O$ of $x$ satisfying $O\subset U$. Local compactness at $x$ gives a compact set $C\subset X$ and an open neighborhood $W$ of $x$ with $W\subset C$. Define
\[
K=C\setminus(O\cap W).
\]
This is compact, being closed in $C$. By the Hausdorff property, there exist disjoint open sets $V_1$ and $V_2$ in $X$ such that $x\in V_1$ and $K\subset V_2$. Set $V=V_1\cap O\cap W$. Then $V$ is a neighborhood of $x$ and $V\subset C$. Since $C$ is compact and $X$ is Hausdorff, $C$ is closed, so $\overline V\subset C$. Since $V\subset V_1$ and $V_2$ is open with $V_1\cap V_2=\varnothing$, we have $\overline V\cap V_2=\varnothing$. Hence
\[
\overline V\subset C\setminus K=O\cap W\subset U.
\]
Finally, $\overline V$ is closed in the compact space $C$, and is therefore compact.
\end{proof}

\[

\[
\overline V\subset C\setminus K=O\cap W\subset U.
\]
